title: Understanding Bias
text: Bias in an estimator is a measure of how far off the estimator is from the true parameter value on average.

title: Bias vs. Variance
text: Remember that bias is different from variance. Bias refers to the systematic error, while variance refers to the variability of the estimator.

hintAnswer: The average difference between theta and hat{theta} over all possible simple random samples from the population.
title: Defining Bias
text: What is the definition of bias in the context of an estimator?
choices: The difference between theta and the value of hat{theta} for a particular sample.
The average difference between theta and hat{theta} computed for each element of the sample.
The average difference between theta and hat{theta} over all possible simple random samples from the population.
The difference between the expected value of theta and the value of hat{theta} for a particular sample.
